collocations: throughout the year｜全年
tip_zh: throughout 强调整段时间或全部范围。

definition_en: having a good result
example1_en: The book fair was successful.
example1_zh: 书展很成功。
example2_en: A bus line is successful when workers arrive on time, not when a photo looks full.
example2_zh: 公交线的成功是工人准时到达，不是照片看起来很挤。
collocations: be successful in｜在……上成功
tip_zh: successful 是形容词；succeed 是动词。

definition_en: a hard stone used for buildings and statues
example1_en: The front steps are white marble.
example1_zh: 门前的台阶是白色大理石。
example2_en: Visitors are asked not to touch the marble, because oil from hands leaves a mark.
example2_zh: 请参观者不要摸大理石，手上的油会留下印子。
collocations: marble floor｜大理石地面 ; marble statue｜大理石雕像
tip_zh: 大理石是不可数的材料。一颗玻璃弹珠才用 a marble。

definition_en: one part of a larger thing
example1_en: Cost is one component of the plan.
example1_zh: 费用是计划的一个部分。
example2_en: A component that students cannot see should still be named.
example2_zh: 学生看不见的部分仍然应当写出来。
collocations: a component of｜……的组成部分
tip_zh: component 可数。

definition_en: an area of study, a topic, or the doer in a sentence
example1_en: History is her favourite subject.
example1_zh: 历史是她最喜欢的学科。
example2_en: The subject of a public meeting should be posted before people are asked to attend.
example2_zh: 公开会议的主题应该在请人参加之前公布。
collocations: school subject｜学校科目 ; change the subject｜换话题
tip_zh: subject 作形容词是“受制的”：be subject to。

definition_en: after noon
example1_en: The club meets at 4 p.m.
example1_zh: 社团下午四点见面。
example2_en: A notice that says 4 p.m. and another that says 16:00 should mean the same bus.
example2_zh: 写着下午四点的通知和写着 16:00 的通知，应当指同一班车。
collocations: 4 p.m.｜下午四点
tip_zh: p.m. 表示中午到午夜。与 pm 是同一个缩写，本库只保留 p.m.，以便和已有的 a.m. 一致。数字和 p.m. 之间留空格。

meanings_zh: n. 蠢人 | v. 欺骗
definition_en: a person who acts unwisely | to trick someone
example1_en: It is unkind to call a classmate a fool.
example1_zh: 把同学叫做蠢人是不友善的。
example2_en: A fool in a story can be funny; a fool aimed at a student is not.
example2_zh: 故事里的傻瓜可以好笑；对着学生说的傻瓜则不是。
collocations: make a fool of｜愚弄
tip_zh: fool 用在人身上会伤人。作动词是欺骗。

definition_en: the first part
example1_en: Read the beginning of the story again.
example1_zh: 把故事的开头再读一遍。
example2_en: The beginning of a heatwave is the time to open cool public rooms, not the day after people collapse.
example2_zh: 热浪开始时就该开放凉爽的公共房间，而不是等人们倒下之后。
collocations: at the beginning of｜在……开始时 ; from the beginning｜从一开始
tip_zh: at the beginning of 后接名词。

definition_en: not clean
example1_en: Do not drink from a dirty cup.
example1_zh: 不要用脏杯子喝水。
example2_en: A dirty filter in the lab is a reason to stop, not to hurry.
example2_zh: 实验室里脏了的滤器是停下来的理由，不是赶工的理由。
collocations: dirty hands｜脏手
tip_zh: dirty 作动词是弄脏。

definition_en: the protection of nature or of something valuable
example1_en: Conservation of water starts with a closed tap.
example1_zh: 节约用水从关好水龙头开始。
example2_en: A conservation plan should name who waters the school garden in August.
example2_zh: 保护计划应当写明八月谁给学校园子浇水。
collocations: conservation of｜对……的保护
tip_zh: conservation 通常不可数。

meanings_zh: v. 适合 | n. 一套衣服
definition_en: to be right for someone or something | a set of clothes
example1_en: The early class does not suit everyone.
example1_zh: 早课并不适合每个人。
example2_en: A timetable that suits the bus also suits the students who cannot stay late.
example2_zh: 适合公交的课表，也适合不能留下来很晚的学生。
collocations: suit sb｜适合某人 ; be suited to｜适合于
tip_zh: suit 作名词是一套衣服。动词是适合。两种读音都常见。

definition_en: the rules of a language
example1_en: The grammar point is on the board.
example1_zh: 这个语法点写在黑板上。
example2_en: Grammar without a real sentence is harder to remember.
example2_zh: 没有真实句子的语法更难记住。
collocations: English grammar｜英语语法
tip_zh: grammar 作学科时常不可数。

definition_en: very foolish, or very enthusiastic
example1_en: It is crazy to cycle without a light at night.
example1_zh: 夜里骑车不带灯是很荒唐的。
example2_en: A crazy building boom can fill a town with flats nobody on a local wage can rent.
example2_zh: 疯狂的建设热潮会让城镇充满本地工资租不起的公寓。
collocations: be crazy about｜对……着迷
tip_zh: crazy 是口语词，正式写作可用 foolish 或 unwise。

definition_en: the sense of perceiving sound, or an official meeting to hear facts
example1_en: The test checks hearing, not only reading.
example1_zh: 这次测验检查听力，不只是阅读。
example2_en: A public hearing lets neighbours speak before a new road is drawn through their street.
example2_zh: 公开听证会让邻居在新路画过他们的街道之前发言。
collocations: hearing loss｜听力损失 ; hard of hearing｜听力不好
tip_zh: 动词 hear 已在本库。hearing 是名词，也可指听证会。

definition_en: two people, or a small number
example1_en: A couple of students stayed to tidy up.
example1_zh: 有几个学生留下来收拾。
example2_en: A young couple may leave a town when the only flats cost more than their wages.
example2_zh: 当仅有的公寓贵过工资时，年轻夫妇可能会离开城镇。
collocations: a couple of｜几个；一对
tip_zh: a couple of 在口语里常表示“几个”，不一定正好两个。

definition_en: permission to enter, or the fee for entering
example1_en: Admission to the hall is free.
example1_zh: 进入礼堂是免费的。
example2_en: Admission rules should say what a family does if they cannot pay.
example2_zh: 入场规定应当写明家庭付不起时怎么办。
collocations: admission to｜进入…… ; admission fee｜入场费
tip_zh: admission 可指允许进入，也可指入场费。

definition_en: a piece of paper that allows you to travel or enter
example1_en: Keep your ticket until you leave the station.
example1_zh: 离开车站前留着票。
example2_en: A free ticket that the last bus cannot honour is not free for the student who must take a taxi.
example2_zh: 末班车用不了的免费票，对必须改乘出租车的学生并不免费。
collocations: a ticket for｜……的票 ; ticket office｜售票处
tip_zh: ticket 可数。交通罚单也叫 ticket。

definition_en: a piece of metal used as money
example1_en: She found a coin under the desk.
example1_zh: 她在书桌下找到一枚硬币。
example2_en: A coin on a poster is not the fee a family can check.
example2_zh: 海报上的硬币不是家庭能核对的费用。
collocations: a gold coin｜一枚金币
tip_zh: coin 可数。

definition_en: a small round mark
example1_en: Put a dot after the number on the map.
example1_zh: 在地图上的数字后面点一个点。
example2_en: Each red dot on the chart is one student who walks to school.
example2_zh: 图表上每个红点代表一名步行上学的学生。
collocations: a dot｜一个点 ; on the dot｜准时
tip_zh: on the dot 表示准时，不是「在点上」。字母 i 上面的一点也叫 dot。

definition_en: the soft part of the body, or the meat of an animal or fruit
example1_en: The flesh of the peach is sweet.
example1_zh: 桃肉是甜的。
example2_en: Cook the flesh of the fish until it is white.
example2_zh: 把鱼肉煮到变白。
collocations: flesh and blood｜血肉之躯
tip_zh: flesh 通常不可数。本条用食物和身体的普通意思。

definition_en: the process of growing
example1_en: The growth of the town has been fast.
example1_zh: 这个城镇增长得很快。
example2_en: Rapid growth along a river can bring jobs and also destroy the wetland that holds flood water.
example2_zh: 河边的快速增长能带来工作，也会毁掉蓄洪水的湿地。
collocations: population growth｜人口增长 ; economic growth｜经济增长
tip_zh: growth 通常不可数。

definition_en: the ability to do something well
example1_en: Checking a source is a skill.
example1_zh: 核对来源是一项技能。
example2_en: A skill that only one student can practise is not yet a class skill.
example2_zh: 只有一个学生能练的技能，还不是全班的技能。
collocations: a skill in｜……方面的技能
tip_zh: skill 可数。表里这一行的音标是 ski，本库不用。

definition_en: something that is done
example1_en: We need action, not only a poster.
example1_zh: 我们需要行动，而不只是一张海报。
example2_en: Climate action in a city includes buses and buildings, not only speeches on a special day.
example2_zh: 一座城市的气候行动包括公交和建筑，而不只是特殊日子里的演讲。
collocations: take action｜采取行动 ; in action｜在运转
tip_zh: take action to do 表示采取行动做某事。

definition_en: a story, often an imagined one
example1_en: The tale is about a late bus.
example1_zh: 这个故事讲的是一趟晚班车。
example2_en: A tale can be fiction, and the bus time on the wall still has to be fact.
example2_zh: 故事可以是虚构的，墙上的公交时间却必须是事实。
collocations: a tale of｜一个……的故事
tip_zh: tale 与 tail（尾巴）同音。tail 已在本库。

meanings_zh: num. 第二；秒 | n. 秒；片刻
definition_en: the one after the first, or a unit of time | a very short time
example1_en: I sat in the second row.
example1_zh: 我坐在第二排。
example2_en: A delay of even a second at a busy junction can add up to long queues in the evening.
example2_zh: 繁忙路口哪怕一秒钟的延误，也会在傍晚累积成长队。
collocations: a second｜再一个 ; second-hand｜二手的
tip_zh: the second 表示顺序；a second 可以表示“又一”。

definition_en: found in many places
example1_en: The practice is widespread in this town.
example1_zh: 这种做法在这座城镇很普遍。
example2_en: Sharing tools is widespread among the farms here.
example2_zh: 在这里的农场之间，共用工具很普遍。
collocations: widespread support｜广泛支持
tip_zh: widespread 只作形容词。

meanings_zh: v. 搜索；搜查 | n. 搜索
definition_en: to look carefully for something | an act of searching
example1_en: Search the website for the bus times.
example1_zh: 在网站上搜索公交时刻。
example2_en: Families search for a flat they can afford near a school, and often fail.
example2_zh: 家庭寻找学校附近租得起的公寓，却常常找不到。
collocations: search for｜寻找 ; in search of｜寻找
tip_zh: search 可直接接地点，search for 后接寻找的对象。

definition_en: something said to make people laugh
example1_en: The joke was kind, and everyone laughed.
example1_zh: 这个玩笑很善意，大家都笑了。
example2_en: A joke about a classmate's name is not funny when that student cannot leave the room.
example2_zh: 拿同学的名字开玩笑，当那个学生没法离开房间时，就不好笑了。
collocations: tell a joke｜讲笑话 ; play a joke on｜捉弄
tip_zh: joke 作动词是开玩笑。make a joke 或 tell a joke 都可以。

definition_en: coming before
example1_en: Look at the previous page.
example1_zh: 看前一页。
example2_en: The previous flood should have changed the building rules, but the same land was sold again.
example2_zh: 上一次洪水本应改变建筑规则，但同一块地又被卖掉了。
collocations: previous to｜在……之前
tip_zh: previous 前面常用 the。

definition_en: a person you invite, or who stays at a hotel
example1_en: The guest spoke for ten minutes.
example1_zh: 客人讲了十分钟。
example2_en: A guest speaker needs a chair, a glass of water, and a way back to the station.
example2_zh: 嘉宾需要一把椅子、一杯水和回车站的办法。
collocations: a guest speaker｜嘉宾
tip_zh: guest 可数。主人是 host，已在本库。

definition_en: a person thought to be guilty
example1_en: The report does not name the suspect.
example1_zh: 报道没有写出嫌疑人的名字。
example2_en: Calling a student a suspect before the facts are written down is not fair.
example2_zh: 在事实写下来之前把学生叫做嫌疑人，是不公平的。
collocations: a suspect in｜……案的嫌疑人
tip_zh: 名词嫌疑人重音常在前。动词“怀疑”重音在后：/səˈspekt/。本条以名词为主，不写办案步骤。

definition_en: a small animal with a long tail
example1_en: A rat got into the store room.
example1_zh: 一只老鼠进了储藏室。
example2_en: They closed the food after they saw the rat.
example2_zh: 他们看见老鼠以后把食物收了起来。
collocations: a rat in｜……里的老鼠
tip_zh: rat 可数。本条不写如何伤害动物。

definition_en: a flat surface that shows images
example1_en: The screen at the back of the lab is new.
example1_zh: 实验室后面的屏幕是新的。
example2_en: A bright screen late at night can delay sleep even when the homework on it is finished.
example2_zh: 即使屏幕上的作业已经写完，深夜亮着的屏幕仍会推迟睡眠。
collocations: on the screen｜在屏幕上 ; screen time｜屏幕时间
tip_zh: screen 也可指纱窗或屏风。看电影的幕布也叫 screen。

definition_en: a person you do an activity with
example1_en: My partner in the lab checked the numbers.
example1_zh: 我的实验搭档核对了数字。
example2_en: A business partner who hides costs can damage a small shop faster than a quiet week.
example2_zh: 隐瞒成本的生意伙伴，对小店的伤害可以超过一周冷清。
collocations: partner with｜与……合作
tip_zh: partner 可以是合作伙伴、舞伴或配偶，要看语境。

definition_en: an object that moves around a planet, or a machine that does so
example1_en: The satellite sends the weather map.
example1_zh: 卫星发送天气图。
example2_en: A satellite picture of the flood still needs someone who can read it.
example2_zh: 洪水的卫星图片仍然需要有人能看懂。
collocations: a satellite of｜……的卫星
tip_zh: satellite 可数。

definition_en: no person
example1_en: Nobody was late today.
example1_zh: 今天没有人迟到。
example2_en: Nobody should have to wait for a bus in the dark if the town can put up one light.
example2_zh: 如果城镇能装一盏灯，就不该有人在黑暗中等公交。
collocations: nobody else｜没有别人
tip_zh: nobody 作主语时谓语用单数。

definition_en: the part of a piece of clothing that covers the arm
example1_en: Ink stained the sleeve of his shirt.
example1_zh: 墨水弄脏了他的衬衫袖子。
example2_en: Roll your sleeve up before the nurse takes your pulse, so the cloth stays clean.
example2_zh: 护士量脉搏前把袖子卷起来，布就不用弄脏。
collocations: shirt sleeve｜衬衫袖 ; roll up one's sleeves｜卷起袖子；准备大干
tip_zh: 袖子是 sleeve。叶子是 leaf。卷起袖子准备干活是 roll up one's sleeves。

definition_en: the land next to the sea
example1_en: We walked along the coast at sunset.
example1_zh: 日落时我们沿着海岸走。
example2_en: Towns on a low coast need a plan for storms before the sea wall fails.
example2_zh: 低海岸上的城镇需要在海堤失事之前就有风暴方案。
collocations: on the coast｜在海岸 ; the coast of｜……的海岸
tip_zh: coast 是较大的海岸地带。shore 更强调水边的岸。

definition_en: to go or come in
example1_en: Enter the lab only with a teacher.
example1_zh: 只有老师在场才能进入实验室。
example2_en: Students who enter a new school in the middle of the year need a map and a person, not only a form.
example2_zh: 学年中途入学的学生需要一张地图和一个人，而不只是一张表。
collocations: enter a room｜进入房间 ; enter for｜报名参加
tip_zh: 进入某处直接说 enter a room，一般不加 into。enter into 多用于“开始讨论”或“达成协议”。

definition_en: a careful examination
example1_en: The analysis of the water will take a week.
example1_zh: 水质分析要一周。
example2_en: An analysis of late arrivals should look at buses before it looks at character.
example2_zh: 对迟到的分析应该先看公交，再看品格。
collocations: analysis of｜对……的分析
tip_zh: analysis 的复数是 analyses。

definition_en: the surface of a room, or a level of a building
example1_en: Please pick up the paper on the floor.
example1_zh: 请把地上的纸捡起来。
example2_en: The library is on the second floor, which is hard to reach without a lift.
example2_zh: 图书馆在二楼，没有电梯很难到达。
collocations: on the floor｜在地板上 ; ground floor｜底层
tip_zh: 英式 ground floor 是一层；美式 first floor 常指一层。

definition_en: land used for growing food or raising animals
example1_en: Her uncle works on a farm outside the town.
example1_zh: 她叔叔在镇外的农场干活。
example2_en: A school that visits a farm should ask who owns the land and who does the work.
example2_zh: 学校参观农场时，应当问土地是谁的、活是谁干的。
collocations: on the farm｜在农场
tip_zh: farm 作动词是务农。

definition_en: not high
example1_en: The shelf is low enough for everyone to reach.
example1_zh: 架子低得每个人都够得着。
example2_en: Low pay in village schools makes it hard to keep teachers who could work in the city.
example2_zh: 乡村学校的低报酬，让那些可以去城市工作的老师很难留下来。
collocations: low price｜低价 ; at a low level｜处于低水平
tip_zh: low 的比较级是 lower。人的声音低用 a low voice。

definition_en: a sign, sound, or movement that sends a message
example1_en: The signal was too weak for the video.
example1_zh: 信号太弱，视频放不了。
example2_en: A green signal at the crossing matters more than a poster about safety.
example2_zh: 路口的绿灯比一张安全海报更重要。
collocations: a signal to｜……的信号 ; mobile signal｜手机信号
tip_zh: signal 作动词是发信号。

definition_en: a formal test, or a careful look
example1_en: The examination is in the hall.
example1_zh: 考试在礼堂。
example2_en: A medical examination should be explained before it starts.
example2_zh: 体检应当在开始前说明。
collocations: an examination of｜对……的检查
tip_zh: 简称 exam 是本批的另一词。表里没有 examination 这一条，本库用 espeak-ng。本条不写检查步骤。

definition_en: a large old building built for defence
example1_en: The castle is on the hill.
example1_zh: 城堡在山上。
example2_en: A castle in a textbook should also say who carried the water.
example2_zh: 课本里的城堡也应当写是谁担的水。
collocations: a castle on｜……上的城堡
tip_zh: castle 可数。

definition_en: very bad
example1_en: The noise was awful during the drill.
example1_zh: 演习时噪音很糟。
example2_en: An awful score on one quiz is information, not a final judgement.
example2_zh: 一次小测的糟糕分数是信息，不是最终判决。
collocations: an awful mistake｜严重的错误
tip_zh: awful 程度很强。awfully 在口语里也可表示“非常”。

definition_en: a picture made with paint
example1_en: The painting hangs in the hall.
example1_zh: 这幅画挂在大厅里。
example2_en: A student painting of the river can teach the town what the bank looks like after rain.
example2_zh: 学生画的河，能让城镇看见雨后的河岸。
collocations: oil painting｜油画
tip_zh: painting 作一幅画时可数。作绘画这项活动时不可数。

definition_en: a sharp yellow paste, or the plant it comes from
example1_en: This mustard is too sharp for me.
example1_zh: 这芥末对我来说太冲了。
example2_en: Add a little mustard to the potato salad if you like a sharper taste, and leave the rest in the jar.
example2_zh: 如果你喜欢更冲的味道，就在土豆沙拉里加一点芥末，剩下的留在罐子里。
collocations: mustard sauce｜芥末酱 ; a jar of mustard｜一罐芥末
tip_zh: mustard 作调味酱时不可数。颜色上的芥末黄就说 mustard yellow。

meanings_zh: n. 文本；课文 | v. 发短信
definition_en: written words | to send a written message by phone
example1_en: Read the text before you answer.
example1_zh: 回答之前先读课文。
example2_en: A text message about a storm helps only if it arrives before the road is already under water.
example2_zh: 关于风暴的短信只有在路还没被水淹之前到达才有帮助。
collocations: text message｜短信 ; the text of｜……的文本
tip_zh: text 作动词是“发短信”。

definition_en: a drawing of an area
example1_en: The map shows the bus stops.
example1_zh: 地图标出了公交站。
example2_en: A map of flood risk helps a town decide which school needs a higher floor.
example2_zh: 洪水风险地图帮助城镇决定哪所学校需要更高的楼层。
collocations: on the map｜在地图上 ; a map of｜……的地图
tip_zh: map 作动词是绘制或详细安排。

definition_en: using electronic devices
example1_en: The electronic clock in the hall is wrong.
example1_zh: 大厅里的电子钟不准。
example2_en: An electronic notice still needs a paper copy when the network fails.
example2_zh: 网络断了的时候，电子通知仍然需要一份纸质副本。
collocations: electronic mail｜电子邮件
tip_zh: electronic 强调电子设备。electric 已在本库，多指用电的。

meanings_zh: v. 移动；搬家；感动 | n. 行动；一步
definition_en: to change place, or to cause a feeling | an action
example1_en: Please move your bag off the seat.
example1_zh: 请把包从座位上移开。
example2_en: Families move away when rents rise faster than wages, and schools then lose students.
example2_zh: 当房租涨得比工资快时，家庭会搬走，学校随后失去学生。
collocations: move to｜搬到 ; move on｜继续前进 ; be moved｜被感动
tip_zh: move 可作及物或不及物。搬家用 move to a place。

definition_en: what happens because of something
example1_en: The result of the test will come out tomorrow.
example1_zh: 考试结果明天出来。
example2_en: The result of cutting night buses is that workers walk home on dark roads.
example2_zh: 削减夜班公交的结果是，工人走在没有灯的路上回家。
collocations: as a result｜因此 ; result in｜导致 ; result from｜由……引起
tip_zh: result in 后接后果；result from 后接原因。

definition_en: to cause something to go somewhere
example1_en: Please send the form to the office.
example1_zh: 请把表格送到办公室。
example2_en: Schools that send warnings only by app miss families who have no signal at home.
example2_zh: 只用应用发送警报的学校，会漏掉家里没有信号的家庭。
collocations: send for｜派人去请 ; send out｜发出
tip_zh: send 的过去式和过去分词是 sent。

definition_en: something you do regularly
example1_en: Checking the source is a habit.
example1_zh: 核对来源是一个习惯。
example2_en: A habit of writing the bus time saves the phone call.
example2_zh: 写下公交时间的习惯能省掉那通电话。
collocations: a habit of｜……的习惯 ; get into a habit｜养成习惯
tip_zh: habit 可数。

definition_en: about, but not exactly
example1_en: The hall holds approximately 200 people.
example1_zh: 大厅大约容纳 200 人。
example2_en: Approximately right numbers are useful, and a budget still needs the exact figure.
example2_zh: 大约正确的数字有用，预算仍然需要确切的数。
collocations: approximately equal｜大约相等
tip_zh: approximately 比 about 正式。

meanings_zh: v. 打勾；滴答响 | n. 勾号；滴答声
definition_en: to mark a box with a tick, or to make a light repeated sound | that mark or that sound
example1_en: Tick the sentences you agree with.
example1_zh: 在你同意的句子旁打勾。
example2_en: A loud tick from the clock made the quiet room feel even quieter after it stopped.
example2_zh: 钟的滴答声很大，它停了以后安静的房间显得更静。
collocations: tick a box｜在方框里打勾 ; the tick of a clock｜钟的滴答声
word_family: tick off (phr. v. 打勾标出)
tip_zh: 英式在方框里打勾是 tick。美式常用 check。不要写成 ticket。

definition_en: stone, or a kind of popular music
example1_en: We sat on a flat rock by the lake.
example1_zh: 我们坐在湖边一块平坦的岩石上。
example2_en: A rock concert in a small square needs a volume that still lets neighbours sleep.
example2_zh: 小广场上的摇滚音乐会需要一个仍让邻居能睡觉的音量。
collocations: rock music｜摇滚乐
tip_zh: rock 作动词是“摇动”。

definition_en: the set of keys on a computer or a piano
example1_en: The keyboard is beside the screen.
example1_zh: 键盘在屏幕旁边。
example2_en: A keyboard in the library still needs a person who can help.
example2_zh: 图书馆里的键盘仍然需要有人能帮忙。
collocations: a computer keyboard｜计算机键盘
tip_zh: keyboard 可数。

definition_en: a strong elastic material, or a tool that removes pencil marks
example1_en: The rubber is on the desk.
example1_zh: 橡皮在书桌上。
example2_en: Rubber boots by the door matter when the path is wet.
example2_zh: 小路湿的时候，门边的胶靴就有用。
collocations: a rubber of｜一块橡皮 ; rubber boots｜胶靴
tip_zh: 英式 rubber 常指橡皮。美式 eraser 更常见。材料“橡胶”通常不可数。

meanings_zh: v. 混合 | n. 混合；混合物
definition_en: to combine different things | a combination
example1_en: Do not mix those two liquids.
example1_zh: 不要把那两种液体混在一起。
example2_en: Cities that mix housing and shops keep a street alive after the offices close.
example2_zh: 把住房和商店混在一起的城市，能让街道在办公室关门后仍然有人。
collocations: mix up｜混淆 ; mix with｜与……混合
tip_zh: mix up 是搞混。a mix of 是名词短语。

definition_en: the power used to make light and machines work
example1_en: The electricity failed during the storm.
example1_zh: 暴风雨时停电了。
example2_en: Electricity from the school roof still needs someone who can repair it.
example2_zh: 学校屋顶发的电，仍然需要有人能修。
collocations: electricity supply｜供电
tip_zh: electricity 不可数。electric 和 electrical 都已在或将在本库。

definition_en: something that is made or grown to be sold
example1_en: The label says where the product comes from.
example1_zh: 标签写明产品来自哪里。
example2_en: A cheap product that cannot be repaired becomes waste faster than a simple tool.
example2_zh: 无法修理的便宜产品，会比一件简单工具更快变成垃圾。
collocations: product of｜……的产品
tip_zh: product 是可数名词。

definition_en: a series of names or items
example1_en: Your name is not on the list.
example1_zh: 名单上没有你的名字。
example2_en: A waiting list for a clinic shows demand, but it does not treat the patient.
example2_zh: 诊所的等候名单显示需求，但并不治疗病人。
collocations: a list of｜一份……清单 ; make a list｜列清单
tip_zh: list 作动词是“列出”。

definition_en: material of threads with spaces, or a network
example1_en: The ball went into the net.
example1_zh: 球进了网。
example2_en: A safety net under the gym equipment prevents one fall from becoming a serious injury.
example2_zh: 体操器械下的安全网，能避免一次跌落变成重伤。
collocations: the Net｜互联网 ; fishing net｜渔网
tip_zh: the Net 可指互联网，和 web 相近。本库已有 network。

definition_en: an opinion, or a decision by a court
example1_en: In my judgement the blue ink is clearer.
example1_zh: 依我看，蓝墨水更清楚。
example2_en: The court's judgement was read aloud, and the class discussed what the words required.
example2_zh: 法庭的判决被宣读出来，全班讨论这些话要求做什么。
collocations: in one's judgement｜依某人看 ; pass judgement｜做出判断；下判决
tip_zh: 英式常拼 judgement。美式 judgment 已在本库。判断和判决都用这个名词。

definition_en: to come together, or to satisfy a need
example1_en: We will meet at the gate at seven.
example1_zh: 我们七点在门口见面。
example2_en: A bus timetable should meet the hour when school ends, not an office hour from another city.
example2_zh: 公交时刻应该配合放学的时间，而不是另一座城市的办公时间。
collocations: meet with｜会见 ; sports meet｜运动会
tip_zh: meet 的过去式和过去分词是 met。初次相识用 meet；重逢也用 meet。

definition_en: a laboratory
example1_en: The lab closes at five.
example1_zh: 实验室五点关门。
example2_en: A lab rule that requires goggles only works if the goggles are there.
example2_zh: 要求戴护目镜的实验室规定，只有护目镜真的在时才有效。
collocations: in the lab｜在实验室 ; lab coat｜实验服
tip_zh: lab 是 laboratory 的缩写。表里这一行的音标是 knowledge，本库不用。

definition_en: as far as you are concerned, or in person
example1_en: Personally, I prefer the early bus.
example1_zh: 就我个人而言，我更喜欢早班车。
example2_en: The head teacher personally checked the lock.
example2_zh: 校长亲自检查了锁。
collocations: personally speaking｜就个人来说
tip_zh: personal 已在本库，并提醒不要和 personnel 拼混。personally 是副词。

definition_en: to remain in a place or state
example1_en: Please stay in your seat until the bell.
example1_zh: 铃响前请留在座位上。
example2_en: Young workers stay in a town only if housing and jobs appear together.
example2_zh: 只有住房和工作同时出现，年轻工人才会留在城镇。
collocations: stay up｜熬夜 ; stay away｜离开 ; stay healthy｜保持健康
tip_zh: stay 作连系动词后接形容词：stay calm。

definition_en: the passage in the neck for food and air
example1_en: Her throat hurt on Monday.
example1_zh: 周一她喉咙疼。
example2_en: A sore throat is a reason to see the clinic before the match.
example2_zh: 喉咙疼是比赛前去医务室的理由。
collocations: a sore throat｜喉咙疼
tip_zh: throat 可数。

definition_en: feeling pleasure
example1_en: I am happy to help with the posters.
example1_zh: 我乐意帮忙做海报。
example2_en: A happy photo of a new park hides the families who were moved to make space for it.
example2_zh: 新公园的快乐照片，藏起了为腾地方而被搬走的家庭。
collocations: be happy to do｜乐意做 ; happy with｜对……满意
tip_zh: happy 后接 to do 或 that 从句。

definition_en: to be brave enough to do something
example1_en: She dared to ask about the fee.
example1_zh: 她敢于询问费用。
example2_en: Do not dare a classmate to do something unsafe.
example2_zh: 不要激同学去做不安全的事。
collocations: dare to do｜敢于做
tip_zh: How dare you 表示“你怎么敢”。本条不写冒险的做法。

meanings_zh: adj. 自信的 | adj. 确信的；有把握的
definition_en: sure of yourself | certain that something is true or will happen
example1_en: Speak in a confident voice.
example1_zh: 用自信的声音说话。
example2_en: Students become more confident when teachers provide constructive feedback and opportunities to practise new skills.
example2_zh: 当教师提供建设性反馈和练习新技能的机会时，学生会变得更自信。
collocations: feel confident｜感到自信 ; confident about the future｜对未来有信心 ; confident that｜确信
tip_zh: confident是形容词；confidence是名词。

definition_en: a sign shaped like an arrow, or a stick shot from a bow
example1_en: The arrow points to the clinic.
example1_zh: 箭头指向诊所。
example2_en: Follow the arrow to the hall.
example2_zh: 顺着箭头走到礼堂。
collocations: an arrow to｜指向……的箭头
tip_zh: 本条以路标为主。不写如何伤人。

meanings_zh: n. 成绩；年级；等级 | v. 评分；分等
definition_en: a mark, a school year, or a level of quality | to give a mark or a level
example1_en: She got a high grade in history.
example1_zh: 她历史成绩很高。
example2_en: A single grade should not decide whether a student may join the choir.
example2_zh: 一个分数不该决定学生能否参加合唱团。
collocations: in the same grade｜同一年级 ; grade A｜甲等
tip_zh: grade 可指分数、年级或品质等级。作动词是评分。

meanings_zh: v. 投；抛 | n. 演员阵容
definition_en: to throw | the actors in a play or film
example1_en: Cast the net carefully from the bank.
example1_zh: 从岸上小心地撒网。
example2_en: The cast of the school play includes students who have never stood on a stage.
example2_zh: 校园剧的演员阵容里有从未上过台的学生。
collocations: cast a vote｜投票 ; cast light on｜阐明
tip_zh: cast 的过去式和过去分词仍是 cast。作名词是“演员阵容”。

meanings_zh: n. 滥用 | v. 滥用；虐待
definition_en: wrong or cruel use | to use wrongly, or to treat cruelly
example1_en: Drug abuse is discussed in health class without any instructions.
example1_zh: 健康课讨论药物滥用，但不提供任何做法。
example2_en: If you see abuse, tell a teacher. You do not have to handle it alone.
example2_zh: 如果你看到虐待，告诉老师。你不必独自处理。
collocations: drug abuse｜药物滥用 ; abuse of｜对……的滥用
tip_zh: 动词 abuse 末尾常读 /z/，名词常读 /s/。本条只作词汇，不写任何伤害别人的方法。

definition_en: things that people or animals eat
example1_en: The food in the canteen was simple but hot.
example1_zh: 食堂的食物简单但是热的。
example2_en: Wasted food in school kitchens is a loss of money and of the water used to grow it.
example2_zh: 学校厨房里浪费的食物，既是金钱的损失，也是种植它所用水的损失。
collocations: fast food｜快餐 ; food and drink｜饮食
tip_zh: food 通常不可数。一种食物可以说 a food，但较少用。

definition_en: sounds arranged in a way people enjoy
example1_en: There is music practice in the hall after school.
example1_zh: 放学后大厅里有音乐排练。
example2_en: Live music in a square can bring a neighbourhood together, but only if the volume lets people talk.
example2_zh: 广场上的现场音乐能把社区聚在一起，但前提是音量仍允许人们交谈。
collocations: pop music｜流行音乐 ; music lesson｜音乐课
tip_zh: music 不可数，不说 a music 或 musics。

definition_en: a person trained in the law who advises and speaks in court
example1_en: The lawyer explained the form in plain words.
example1_zh: 律师用平实的话解释了表格。
example2_en: A school does not need a lawyer for every rule, but it does need one clear written policy.
example2_zh: 学校不是每条规则都需要律师，但确实需要一份写清楚的制度。
collocations: a lawyer for｜……的律师
tip_zh: lawyer 可数。法律是 law，已在本库。

meanings_zh: n. 商店；贮存 | v. 储存
definition_en: a shop, or a supply kept for later | to keep something for future use
example1_en: The store on the corner sells notebooks.
example1_zh: 拐角的商店卖笔记本。
example2_en: A village store that closes forces families to travel for food they used to buy next door.
example2_zh: 村里的商店关门后，家庭不得不为过去在隔壁就能买到的食物出远门。
collocations: department store｜百货商店 ; in store｜即将发生
tip_zh: store 作动词是“储存”。美式 store 常指商店。

definition_en: a round part that turns
example1_en: The wheel of the cart is loose.
example1_zh: 手推车的轮子松了。
example2_en: A wheelchair needs a path, not only a poster about welcome.
example2_zh: 轮椅需要一条路，而不只是一张欢迎海报。
collocations: behind the wheel｜在驾驶
tip_zh: wheel 可数。wheelchair 是轮椅。

definition_en: the money spent on something
example1_en: The expense is written on the form.
example1_zh: 费用写在表格上。
example2_en: An expense that families cannot see is not a fair price.
example2_zh: 家庭看不见的费用不是公平的价格。
collocations: at the expense of｜以牺牲……为代价
tip_zh: expense 可数也可不可数。

definition_en: a set of pages on the internet
example1_en: The bus times are on the school website.
example1_zh: 公交时刻在学校网站上。
example2_en: A website that hides who wrote a story makes it harder to trust the facts.
example2_zh: 隐瞒作者的网站，让人更难信任其中的事实。
collocations: visit a website｜访问网站
tip_zh: website 是一个词，也可写成 web site。

meanings_zh: n. 电话 | v. 打电话
definition_en: a phone | to speak to someone by phone
example1_en: The telephone is by the office door.
example1_zh: 电话在办公室门边。
example2_en: A telephone number on the wall matters when the network fails.
example2_zh: 网络断了的时候，墙上的电话号码很重要。
collocations: by telephone｜通过电话 ; telephone number｜电话号码
tip_zh: phone 已在本库，更常用。表里这一行的音标是 telegraph，本库不用。

meanings_zh: n. 问题 | v. 质疑
definition_en: something you ask | to express doubt about
example1_en: May I ask a question about the homework?
example1_zh: 我可以问一个关于作业的问题吗？
example2_en: The right question about a new road is who will walk it, not only how many cars it will carry.
example2_zh: 关于一条新路，正确的问题是谁会在上面走，而不只是它能载多少车。
collocations: ask a question｜提问 ; out of the question｜不可能 ; in question｜讨论中的
tip_zh: out of the question 是“不可能”；out of question 现在很少用。

definition_en: despite the fact that
example1_en: Though the lab is small, the equipment is new.
example1_zh: 虽然实验室小，设备却是新的。
example2_en: Though a city plants trees, the streets stay hot if the trees are too young to give shade.
example2_zh: 尽管一座城市种了树，如果树还小、遮不成荫，街道依然炎热。
collocations: even though｜即使 ; as though｜好像
tip_zh: though 可放在句首或句末；although 多放在句首，一般不放句末。

definition_en: the force of pushing, or stress
example1_en: Exam pressure is common in the last month.
example1_zh: 最后一个月考试压力很常见。
example2_en: Pressure to publish quickly can make a newsroom skip the check that would catch a false photo.
example2_zh: 赶快发表的压力，会让编辑部跳过能发现假照片的核对。
collocations: under pressure｜在压力下 ; blood pressure｜血压
tip_zh: pressure 通常不可数。put pressure on sb 表示向某人施压。

definition_en: if, used when there are two possibilities
example1_en: I do not know whether the museum is open.
example1_zh: 我不知道博物馆是否开着。
example2_en: Whether a town keeps its clinic depends on buses as well as on doctors.
example2_zh: 一个城镇能否保住诊所，既取决于医生，也取决于公交。
collocations: whether...or｜是……还是 ; whether or not｜是否
tip_zh: whether 可接不定式：whether to go。if 一般不接不定式。介词后用 whether，不用 if。

definition_en: a person who lives next to you; American spelling
example1_en: The neighbor watered the plants.
example1_zh: 邻居给植物浇了水。
example2_en: The neighbor lent us a ladder without being asked.
example2_zh: 邻居没等我们开口就借来了梯子。
collocations: a next-door neighbor｜隔壁邻居
tip_zh: neighbor 是美式，neighbour 是英式。本库词头用考纲里的 neighbor。

meanings_zh: n. 男推销员；男售货员
definition_en: a man whose job is to sell goods
example1_en: The salesman explained the warranty.
example1_zh: 售货员说明了保修条款。
example2_en: A travelling salesman used to carry samples from town to town, which the history unit describes without nostalgia.
example2_zh: 从前的旅行推销员把样品从一个镇带到另一个镇，历史单元只作描述，并不美化。
collocations: a car salesman｜汽车推销员 ; salesman of the month｜本月最佳销售员
word_family: saleswoman (n. 女推销员) ; salesperson (n. 销售员) ; sales (n. 销售)
tip_zh: salesman 专指男性。性别不明时用 salesperson。复数是 salesmen，不要写成 salesmans。

definition_en: a very small town in the countryside
example1_en: Her grandparents live in a village.
example1_zh: 她的祖父母住在一个村子里。
example2_en: A village school with one teacher still has to cover every subject on the exam list.
example2_zh: 只有一位老师的乡村学校，仍然要覆盖考试清单上的每一科。
collocations: in the village｜在村里
tip_zh: village 比 town 小。乡村地区也可说 the village。

definition_en: extremely good
example1_en: The concert was fantastic.
example1_zh: 音乐会棒极了。
example2_en: A fantastic score for one class does not show what the school did for the others.
example2_zh: 一个班的极好成绩，说明不了学校为其他班做了什么。
collocations: a fantastic idea｜极好的主意
tip_zh: fantastic 已经程度很高，口语里很常见。表里没有这一条，本库用 espeak-ng。

definition_en: a movable barrier, or the entrance to a school or airport
example1_en: Meet me at the school gate.
example1_zh: 在校门口等我。
example2_en: A gate that locks before the last student leaves is not a safety plan.
example2_zh: 在最后一名学生离开之前就锁上的门，不是安全方案。
collocations: at the gate｜在门口 ; school gate｜校门
tip_zh: gate 可数。机场登机口也叫 gate。

definition_en: AIDS, a serious illness
example1_en: The health class explains AIDS as an illness.
example1_zh: 健康课把艾滋病作为一种疾病来讲。
example2_en: A poster about AIDS should give facts, not fear.
example2_zh: 关于艾滋病的海报应当给事实，而不是恐惧。
collocations: AIDS prevention｜艾滋病预防
tip_zh: 书写常用大写 AIDS。本条是健康词汇，不写传播或治疗的做法。

definition_en: new information about events
example1_en: The news about the match spread quickly.
example1_zh: 关于比赛的消息很快传开了。
example2_en: Good news reporting explains what is known and what is still uncertain.
example2_zh: 好的新闻报道会说明哪些是已知的，哪些仍不确定。
collocations: a piece of news｜一则新闻 ; news report｜新闻报道
tip_zh: news 不可数，不说 a news。一则新闻用 a piece of news。

definition_en: the name of a book or a person's rank
example1_en: Write a clear title for the poster.
example1_zh: 给海报写一个清楚的标题。
example2_en: The title of a report should say what was measured, not only what sounds impressive.
example2_zh: 报告的标题应该说明测量了什么，而不只是听起来动人。
collocations: job title｜职务名称
tip_zh: title 作动词是“给……加标题”。

definition_en: a raised flat surface, or a place to speak or build on
example1_en: The train leaves from platform two.
example1_zh: 火车从二号站台开出。
example2_en: A platform for student writing needs an editor, not only a website.
example2_zh: 学生写作的平台需要编辑，而不只是一个网站。
collocations: on the platform｜在站台上 ; platform for｜……的平台
tip_zh: 火车站台和演讲台、软件平台都可以用 platform。

definition_en: the act of leaving a vehicle, or space for it
example1_en: There is no parking at the gate.
example1_zh: 门口不能停车。
example2_en: Parking for the bus matters more than parking for one car.
example2_zh: 给公交的停车位比给一辆小汽车的更重要。
collocations: no parking｜禁止停车 ; a parking lot｜停车场
tip_zh: 动词 park 已在本库。parking 通常不可数。

definition_en: to take the place of, or to put something back
example1_en: The new clock will replace the broken one.
example1_zh: 新钟将换掉坏的那一个。
example2_en: Screens do not replace a teacher who knows the student is lost.
example2_zh: 屏幕代替不了知道学生没跟上的老师。
collocations: replace sth with｜用……替换
tip_zh: replace A with B 是用 B 替换 A。

definition_en: a unit of language
example1_en: I wrote the new word in my notebook.
example1_zh: 我把生词写在笔记本里。
example2_en: A single word in a headline can change how readers judge a whole event.
example2_zh: 标题里的一个词就能改变读者对整件事的判断。
collocations: in other words｜换句话说 ; keep one's word｜守信 ; word for word｜逐字
tip_zh: have a word with sb 是和某人说句话；have words with 是争吵。

definition_en: a person who performs in public
example1_en: The youngest performer forgot no line.
example1_zh: 最小的表演者一句词也没忘。
example2_en: Each performer bows once, then leaves the side door so the next act can begin.
example2_zh: 每位表演者鞠一次躬，再从侧门下去，好让下一个节目开始。
collocations: a street performer｜街头艺人 ; the lead performer｜主角
word_family: perform (v. 表演) ; performance (n. 表演) ; performing (adj. 表演的)
tip_zh: performer 包括演员、乐手、杂技演员。动词 perform，名词 performance。

definition_en: an area next to a building, or a unit of length
example1_en: The class meets in the yard.
example1_zh: 班级在院子里集合。
example2_en: A yard with no light is a poor place to wait for the last bus.
example2_zh: 没有灯的院子，是等末班车的糟糕地方。
collocations: in the yard｜在院子里 ; school yard｜校园
tip_zh: yard 作长度是码，约 0.91 米。美式 backyard 是后院。

meanings_zh: adj. 黑暗的 | n. 黑暗
definition_en: with little or no light | the absence of light
example1_en: The street is dark after eight.
example1_zh: 八点以后这条街很黑。
example2_en: A dark walk from the bus stop to the school gate is a safety problem, not a small inconvenience.
example2_zh: 从车站走到校门的一段黑路是安全问题，不是小不便。
collocations: in the dark｜在黑暗中 ; after dark｜天黑以后
tip_zh: dark 也可作名词，前面常加 the。

definition_en: on or onto a ship, plane, or vehicle
example1_en: The students are aboard the bus.
example1_zh: 学生们已经上了公交。
example2_en: Welcome aboard is a greeting, not proof that a seat exists.
example2_zh: Welcome aboard 是一句问候，不是座位存在的证明。
collocations: go aboard｜上船；上车
tip_zh: aboard 是副词或介词，前面常不再加 on。

definition_en: numbers that give information, or the study of them
example1_en: The statistics show who uses the late bus.
example1_zh: 统计数字显示谁在坐晚班车。
example2_en: Statistics without a source are just another opinion.
example2_zh: 没有来源的统计数字只是另一种意见。
collocations: statistics show｜统计显示
tip_zh: 作“统计学”时谓语常用单数。作“统计数字”时谓语用复数。

meanings_zh: n. 土地；陆地 | v. 着陆；登陆
definition_en: ground, or the solid part of the earth | to come down onto the ground
example1_en: The school sits on flat land near the river.
example1_zh: 学校坐落在河边的平地上。
example2_en: Cheap land beside a river looks useful until the first flood shows why it was empty.
example2_zh: 河边的廉价土地看起来有用，直到第一次洪水说明它为什么曾经空着。
collocations: on land｜在陆地上 ; land on｜降落在
tip_zh: land 作动词是“着陆”或“登陆”。

definition_en: the keeping of things until they are needed
example1_en: There is no storage for the extra chairs.
example1_zh: 没有地方存放多余的椅子。
example2_en: Cold storage for milk matters more than a new sign on the canteen door.
example2_zh: 牛奶的冷藏比食堂门上的新牌子更重要。
collocations: in storage｜存放着 ; storage space｜储存空间
tip_zh: storage 通常不可数。store 已在本库。

definition_en: how long something is
example1_en: Measure the length of the table first.
example1_zh: 先量桌子的长度。
example2_en: The length of a school day changes how much daylight children still have for sport.
example2_zh: 上课日的长度会改变孩子放学后还剩多少日光可以运动。
collocations: in length｜长度为 ; at length｜详细地
tip_zh: 长度用 length。at length 是书面语，表示详尽地。

definition_en: pleased
example1_en: I am glad to see you back at school.
example1_zh: 看到你回学校我很高兴。
example2_en: Parents are glad when a late bus is explained, even if the delay itself cannot be avoided.
example2_zh: 即使晚点本身无法避免，只要有人解释，家长也会高兴一些。
collocations: glad to do｜乐意做 ; glad that｜为……高兴
tip_zh: glad 作表语，一般不说 a glad person。

meanings_zh: adj. 最高的；至高无上的
definition_en: highest in rank or greatest
example1_en: The supreme rule here is to lock the lab.
example1_zh: 这里的最高规定是锁好实验室。
example2_en: A supreme court decision can change what a textbook is allowed to say.
example2_zh: 最高法院的裁决可以改变课本被允许写的内容。
collocations: the Supreme Court｜最高法院
tip_zh: supreme 程度已经最高，一般不再加 most。

meanings_zh: v. 发光；照耀 | n. 光亮
definition_en: to give out light, or to be bright | brightness
example1_en: The lamp will shine on the map.
example1_zh: 灯会照在地图上。
example2_en: The sun will shine after the rain.
example2_zh: 雨停后太阳会照出来。
collocations: shine on｜照在
tip_zh: 过去式常用 shone。shine 作名词是光亮。

definition_en: to know someone or something again, or to accept that something is true
example1_en: I did not recognize her in the hat.
example1_zh: 她戴着帽子，我没认出她。
example2_en: A city should recognize a flood risk before the first street is under water.
example2_zh: 城市应当在第一条街被淹之前承认洪水风险。
collocations: recognize sb as｜承认某人是
tip_zh: recognize 是美式拼写。英式常作 recognise。意思相同。

meanings_zh: n. 震惊 | v. 使震惊
definition_en: a sudden strong surprise | to surprise and upset someone
example1_en: The result was a shock.
example1_zh: 这个结果令人震惊。
example2_en: The shock of a cancelled bus is smaller if the other route is already on the sheet.
example2_zh: 如果另一条路线已经写在纸上，公交取消带来的震惊就会小一些。
collocations: a shock to｜对……是震惊 ; in shock｜震惊中
tip_zh: shock 作动词是使震惊。electric shock 是电击，本条不写如何触电。

definition_en: probable
example1_en: Rain is likely today.
example1_zh: 今天可能下雨。

definition_en: going far down, or strong
example1_en: Do not swim where the river is deep.
example1_zh: 河水深的地方不要游泳。
example2_en: Deep floods reach streets that a shallow rain never touches.
example2_zh: 深的洪水会漫到浅雨从不到达的街道。
collocations: deep in｜埋头于 ; deep sleep｜熟睡
tip_zh: deep 可形容水、颜色、睡眠或感情。

definition_en: the crime of stealing
example1_en: The novel mentions a theft and then stops.
example1_zh: 小说提到一次盗窃，然后就停住了。
example2_en: The theft happened on a Sunday.
example2_zh: 这次盗窃发生在星期天。
collocations: report a theft｜报告失窃
tip_zh: theft 可数也可不可数。本条不写方法。

definition_en: a sign that someone may be ill
example1_en: A fever can be a symptom.
example1_zh: 发烧可能是一种症状。
example2_en: Report every symptom to the clinic, including a sore throat, so the nurse can decide the next step.
example2_zh: 每种症状都要告诉校医室，包括嗓子疼，护士才能决定下一步。
collocations: show a symptom｜表现出一种症状 ; flu symptoms｜流感症状
tip_zh: symptom 是疾病表现出来的迹象。原因是 cause。复数 symptoms 很常见。

definition_en: a round vegetable that grows underground
example1_en: The potato is in the soup.
example1_zh: 土豆在汤里。
example2_en: A potato left in the sun is not the lunch the afternoon class needs.
example2_zh: 放在太阳下的土豆不是下午班级需要的午餐。
collocations: a baked potato｜烤土豆
tip_zh: 复数是 potatoes。

definition_en: a play or film that is meant to be funny
example1_en: The comedy made the hall laugh.
example1_zh: 这部喜剧让礼堂里的人笑了。
example2_en: A comedy about a flood can still name who had to leave their house.
example2_zh: 关于洪水的喜剧仍然可以写出谁不得不离开自己的家。
collocations: a comedy about｜关于……的喜剧
tip_zh: comedy 可数。喜剧演员是 comedian。

meanings_zh: n. 间谍 | v. 暗中侦察
definition_en: a person who secretly collects information for a government or company | to watch secretly
example1_en: The novel has a spy, and then it returns to school.
example1_zh: 小说里有一个间谍，然后回到学校。
example2_en: A history text can name a spy without teaching a method.
example2_zh: 历史课文可以提到间谍，同时不教做法。
collocations: a spy for｜为……工作的间谍
tip_zh: spy 作动词是暗中侦察。本条只作词汇，不写做法。

definition_en: at once
example1_en: Please come to the office immediately.
example1_zh: 请立刻到办公室来。
example2_en: A leaking gas pipe should be reported immediately, not after the next lesson.
example2_zh: 煤气管道泄漏应该立刻报告，而不是等下一节课之后。
collocations: immediately after｜在……之后立刻
tip_zh: immediately 是副词；immediate 是形容词。

definition_en: a short piece of writing on a subject
example1_en: The essay is due on Friday.
example1_zh: 短文周五交。
example2_en: An essay about the bus should include the return time.
example2_zh: 写公交的短文应当包括返回时间。
collocations: an essay on｜关于……的短文
tip_zh: essay 可数。

definition_en: to change words into another language
example1_en: Please translate the title into Chinese.
example1_zh: 请把标题译成中文。
example2_en: Do not translate every word; keep the meaning and write a natural sentence.
example2_zh: 不必逐词翻译；保住意思，写成一句自然的话。
collocations: translate into｜译成 ; translate from｜由…译出
tip_zh: translate sth into a language。译文是 translation。

definition_en: a place where adults buy drinks; British
example1_en: The bus stops near the pub.
example1_zh: 公交停在酒吧附近。
example2_en: A pub on a map is a landmark, not an invitation.
example2_zh: 地图上的酒吧是地标，不是邀请。
collocations: at the pub｜在酒吧
tip_zh: pub 是英式。本条只作地点词汇。

definition_en: a child
example1_en: The kid by the gate is waiting for his sister.
example1_zh: 门口的小孩在等他姐姐。
example2_en: A kid walking home in the dark needs a light on the street, not only a lecture about safety.
example2_zh: 在黑暗中走回家的小孩需要街上的灯，而不只是关于安全的说教。
collocations: kids｜孩子们
tip_zh: kid 是口语。正式写作多用 child。

meanings_zh: n. 努力 | n. 尝试；有组织的行动
definition_en: hard work | an attempt or organised activity intended to achieve a goal
example1_en: Success needs continuous effort.
example1_zh: 成功需要持续努力。
example2_en: Reducing household waste requires a joint effort from consumers, manufacturers and local authorities to change everyday practices.
example2_zh: 减少家庭垃圾需要消费者、制造商和地方政府共同努力，改变日常做法。
collocations: make an effort｜作出努力 ; put effort into｜投入精力于 ; a joint effort｜共同努力 ; considerable effort｜相当大的努力
tip_zh: 表示精力时不可数；表示一次尝试时可数。

definition_en: to be in charge, or to succeed in doing something difficult
example1_en: She managed to catch the last bus.
example1_zh: 她设法赶上了末班车。
example2_en: Schools manage a flood better when the plan names a person, not only a building.
example2_zh: 当方案写明一个人而不只是一栋楼时，学校能更好地应对洪水。
collocations: manage to do｜设法做成 ; manage a team｜管理团队
tip_zh: manage to do 表示做成了难事。manager 已在本库。

definition_en: a travelling show with acrobats and clowns
example1_en: A circus tent rose in the park on Friday.
example1_zh: 星期五，公园里支起了马戏团的帐篷。
example2_en: Three classes visited the circus and wrote about the acrobats, not the souvenirs.
example2_zh: 三个班去看了马戏，写的是杂技演员，不是纪念品。
collocations: a circus tent｜马戏团帐篷 ; circus performer｜马戏演员
tip_zh: circus 是演出团体或那场演出。圆形广场才是 circle。

definition_en: a person who visits a place on holiday
example1_en: The tourist bought a map at the station.
example1_zh: 游客在车站买了一张地图。
example2_en: The tourist asked three people before finding the museum.
example2_zh: 游客问了三个人才找到博物馆。
collocations: a tourist from｜来自……的游客
tip_zh: tourism 已在本库。

definition_en: a device that supplies electricity
example1_en: The battery in the clock is dead.
example1_zh: 钟里的电池没电了。
example2_en: A spare battery for the school bus radio matters on a storm day.
example2_zh: 暴风雨那天，校车无线电的备用电池很重要。
collocations: a battery of｜一系列
tip_zh: battery 可数。复数 batteries。

definition_en: different from what is usual or expected
example1_en: An abnormal result must be checked again.
example1_zh: 反常的结果必须再查一次。
example2_en: The temperature was abnormal for April, so the coach shortened the run.
example2_zh: 四月里这个气温不正常，教练就把跑步缩短了。
collocations: abnormal behaviour｜反常行为 ; an abnormal reading｜异常读数
word_family: abnormality (n. 异常) ; normally (adv. 正常地)
tip_zh: abnormal 的反义是 normal。名词 abnormality。不要用它给人贴标签。

definition_en: things for sale or transport
example1_en: The goods arrived before the shop opened.
example1_zh: 货物在商店开门前到了。
example2_en: Goods left in the rain outside a school shop are nobody's bargain.
example2_zh: 放在学校小卖部外淋雨的货物，谁买了都不划算。
collocations: goods train｜货车
tip_zh: goods 是复数，不说 a goods。表里这一行的音标是 good，本库不用。

definition_en: a frozen sweet food
example1_en: We had ice cream after the match.
example1_zh: 比赛后我们吃了冰淇淋。
example2_en: Ice cream left in the sun is not a treat; it is a mess and a risk.
example2_zh: 放在太阳下的冰淇淋不是款待，是一片狼藉，也是风险。
collocations: a bowl of ice cream｜一碗冰淇淋
tip_zh: cream 已在本库。ice cream 通常不可数。an ice cream 可指一份。

definition_en: in a short time
example1_en: The meeting will start soon.
example1_zh: 会议很快就要开始。
example2_en: A leaking roof will soon damage books if a school waits for a perfect budget.
example2_zh: 如果学校一直等一份完美的预算，漏雨的屋顶很快会损坏书籍。
collocations: as soon as｜一……就 ; sooner or later｜迟早
tip_zh: as soon as 引导时间从句，主句将来时，从句用一般现在时。

definition_en: to give a document to someone in authority
example1_en: Submit the form before Friday.
example1_zh: 周五前提交表格。
example2_en: Students submit better work when the question is clear.
example2_zh: 问题清楚时，学生交上来的作业更好。
collocations: submit sth to｜把某物提交给
tip_zh: submit 比 hand in 正式。

meanings_zh: v. 提倡 | n. 倡导者
definition_en: to support an idea in public | a person who supports an idea
example1_en: The club advocates a later library hour.
example1_zh: 社团提倡图书馆晚一点关门。
example2_en: People who advocate a new road should also say who loses the path.
example2_zh: 提倡修新路的人，也应当说出谁会失去原来的小路。
collocations: advocate doing｜提倡做
tip_zh: 动词末音节是 /eɪt/，名词“倡导者”末音节是 /ət/。重音都在第一个音节。

definition_en: a piece of a whole, or a role
example1_en: This chapter is the hardest part of the book.
example1_zh: 这一章是书里最难的部分。
example2_en: Parents are only one part of a child's education; streets, screens, and friends shape habits too.
example2_zh: 父母只是孩子教育的一部分；街道、屏幕和朋友也会塑造习惯。
collocations: take part in｜参加 ; play a part｜起作用 ; part of｜……的一部分
tip_zh: take part in 表示参加活动，不要漏掉 in。

meanings_zh: v. 浪费 | n. 废物；浪费
definition_en: to use something carelessly | unwanted material, or careless use
example1_en: Do not waste paper on a second cover.
example1_zh: 不要为了再做一个封面浪费纸。
example2_en: Food waste from the canteen can feed a garden if someone sorts it the same day.
example2_zh: 如果有人当天分类，食堂的食物废料可以供给花园。
collocations: a waste of｜对……的浪费 ; waste time｜浪费时间
tip_zh: waste 作名词是废物或浪费。food waste 里 waste 可以是名词。

definition_en: the leader of a country, club, or some universities
example1_en: The club president will speak first.
example1_zh: 社团主席将首先发言。
example2_en: A student president who only repeats teachers ideas will not represent the class.
example2_zh: 只重复老师想法的学生主席，代表不了班级。
collocations: vice president｜副总统；副主席
tip_zh: president 在不同机构里可以是总统、主席或大学校长。

definition_en: to make feelings or ideas known, or to carry something
example1_en: Her drawing can convey calm.
example1_zh: 她的画能传达出平静。
example2_en: Trucks convey the books to the county library, while the letters convey the mayor's thanks.
example2_zh: 卡车把书运到县图书馆，信则传达市长的谢意。
collocations: convey a feeling｜传达感情 ; convey goods｜运送货物
word_family: conveyor (n. 传送带) ; conveyance (n. 运送)
tip_zh: 传达想法、感情用 convey sth to sb。传送带是 conveyor belt。

definition_en: to promise to do something, or to do something wrong
example1_en: Please commit to locking the lab.
example1_zh: 请承诺锁上实验室。
example2_en: Do not commit the same error on the next form.
example2_zh: 不要在下一张表上再犯同样的错误。
collocations: commit to｜承诺 ; commit an error｜犯错误
tip_zh: 名词 commitment 已在本库。本条不写伤害自己或他人的做法。

definition_en: a person's own nature or identity
example1_en: The exercise asks you to describe your self in three words.
example1_zh: 这个练习请你用三个词描述自己。
example2_en: A sense of self grows when students are trusted with real tasks, not only with tests.
example2_zh: 当学生被托付真正的任务而不只是考试时，自我意识会成长。
collocations: self-control｜自制 ; yourself｜你自己
tip_zh: self 常构成复合词，如 self-study。复数是 selves。

meanings_zh: prep. 围绕；大约 | adv. 周围；到处
definition_en: on all sides of, or about | in the surrounding area
example1_en: We walked around the lake after lunch.
example1_zh: 午饭后我们绕着湖走了走。
example2_en: Shops around a school gate affect what students buy between classes, from water to sweets.
example2_zh: 校门口的商店影响着学生课间买什么，从水到糖果都是。
collocations: around the world｜全世界 ; look around｜环顾
tip_zh: around 表示大约时与 about 接近：around 20 students。

definition_en: sleeping
example1_en: The baby was asleep on the bus.
example1_zh: 婴儿在公交上睡着了。
example2_en: A student asleep in class may need sleep, not a punishment.
example2_zh: 课上睡着的学生可能需要的是睡眠，不是惩罚。
collocations: fall asleep｜入睡
tip_zh: asleep 只作表语。sleep 已在本库。

definition_en: a person who reports news
example1_en: The reporter checked the name.
example1_zh: 记者核对了名字。
example2_en: A reporter who names no source is harder to trust.
example2_zh: 不写来源的记者更难信任。
collocations: a reporter for｜……的记者
tip_zh: report 已在本库。journalist 是本批的另一词。

definition_en: a female ruler, or the wife of a king
example1_en: The queen visited the old harbour in the story.
example1_zh: 故事里女王参观了古老的港口。
example2_en: A history chapter about a queen should also say who cooked, farmed and paid the taxes.
example2_zh: 写女王的历史章节，也应当说谁在做饭、种地和纳税。
collocations: queen of｜……女王
tip_zh: queen 可以是女性君主，也可以是国王的妻子。

meanings_zh: n. 气味 | v. 闻；发出气味
definition_en: what you notice with your nose | to notice a smell, or to have one
example1_en: There is a smell of paint in the hall.
example1_zh: 大厅里有油漆味。
example2_en: A bad smell from the kitchen is a reason to stop lunch, not to hide it.
example2_zh: 厨房的异味是停下午饭的理由，不是把它藏起来。
collocations: the smell of｜……的气味 ; smell of｜有……的气味
tip_zh: smell 作动词的过去式是 smelt 或 smelled。smell 可作连系动词：smell good。

definition_en: work, especially physical work; British spelling
example1_en: Harvest labour starts before sunrise.
example1_zh: 收割的劳动在日出前就开始了。
example2_en: Child labour is illegal, and a weekend school job is not the same thing.
example2_zh: 童工是非法的，周末在学校打工不是一回事。
collocations: manual labour｜体力劳动
tip_zh: labour 是英式拼写，labor 是美式。考纲里两种都有，本库两条都保留，意思相同。

definition_en: kind and pleasant
example1_en: The staff were friendly to the new students.
example1_zh: 工作人员对新同学很友好。
example2_en: A friendly match still needs a referee and a way home.
example2_zh: 友谊赛仍然需要裁判和回家的办法。
collocations: be friendly to｜对……友好 ; a friendly match｜友谊赛
tip_zh: friendly 是形容词，不是副词。友好地用 in a friendly way。friend 已在本库。

definition_en: the science of matter and energy
example1_en: Physics is the first lesson on Tuesday.
example1_zh: 周二第一节是物理。
example2_en: A physics problem about the bus is more useful than a number with no story.
example2_zh: 一道关于公交的物理题，比一个没有情境的数字更有用。
collocations: physics lab｜物理实验室
tip_zh: physics 作学科时谓语用单数。physical 已在本库。

definition_en: measuring a lot from side to side
example1_en: The new pavement is wide enough for two people.
example1_zh: 新的人行道宽得够两个人走。
example2_en: A wide road without a crossing is still a barrier for a child.
example2_zh: 没有过街处的宽路，对孩子仍然是障碍。
collocations: wide range｜广泛的范围
tip_zh: wide 强调横向的宽；broad 常强调幅面或抽象的广。

definition_en: something accepted as true
example1_en: Strong belief can give people hope.
example1_zh: 坚定的信念能给人希望。
example2_en: The belief that education improves social mobility influences government spending priorities in many countries.
example2_zh: 教育能促进社会流动的这一信念影响着许多国家的政府支出重点。
collocations: belief in someone｜对某人的信任 ; religious beliefs｜宗教信仰 ; a widely held belief｜普遍持有的看法 ; contrary to popular belief｜与普遍看法相反
tip_zh: belief in表示信任或信仰；belief that后接具体看法。

definition_en: to get ready
example1_en: Prepare the lab before the class arrives.
example1_zh: 班级到来之前把实验室准备好。
example2_en: Cities should prepare flood plans before the rainy season, not after the first street is under water.
example2_zh: 城市应当在雨季之前准备防汛方案，而不是等第一条街被淹之后。
collocations: prepare for｜为……做准备 ; prepare to do｜准备做
tip_zh: prepare for 后接所准备的事。prepare sth 是把某物准备好。

meanings_zh: v. 飞；飞行 | n. 苍蝇
definition_en: to move through the air | a small flying insect
example1_en: Birds fly over the sports field.
example1_zh: 鸟飞过运动场。
example2_en: A town that wants fewer cars cannot only tell people to fly; most journeys are short.
example2_zh: 想减少汽车的城镇不能只叫人坐飞机，大多数行程都很短。
collocations: fly a kite｜放风筝
tip_zh: fly 的过去式是 flew，过去分词是 flown。航班名词 flight 已在本库。

definition_en: what you plan to do
example1_en: Her intention is to return the book.
example1_zh: 她的打算是还书。
example2_en: A good intention still needs a written time.
example2_zh: 好意仍然需要一个写下来的时间。
collocations: intention to do｜做……的打算
tip_zh: intention 可数。

definition_en: damaged by use, or very tired
example1_en: The coat is worn at the elbows.
example1_zh: 外套的肘部磨旧了。
example2_en: A worn step should be repaired before someone falls.
example2_zh: 磨坏的台阶应当在有人摔倒之前修好。
collocations: worn out｜疲惫不堪；用坏
tip_zh: worn 是 wear 的过去分词。wear 已在本库。表里把 worm 的读音混了进来，本库不用。

definition_en: demanding that rules are obeyed
example1_en: The rule is strict about the lab door.
example1_zh: 这条规则对实验室的门很严格。
example2_en: A strict timetable still fails if it hides the last bus.
example2_zh: 严格的课表如果藏起末班车，仍然会失败。
collocations: strict with｜对……严格 ; strict about｜对……严格
tip_zh: strict 可形容人或规则。

definition_en: far from towns
example1_en: The village is remote, but the school is open.
example1_zh: 村子很偏远，但学校开着。
example2_en: A remote school still needs a bus, not only a website.
example2_zh: 偏远的学校仍然需要公交，而不只是一个网站。
collocations: a remote area｜偏远地区 ; remote control｜遥控器
tip_zh: remote control 是遥控器。

definition_en: a room where people wait
example1_en: Please stay in the waiting room until your name is called.
example1_zh: 请在候诊室等到叫你的名字。
example2_en: A crowded waiting room shows that a clinic needs more staff, not only more chairs.
example2_zh: 拥挤的候诊室说明诊所需要更多工作人员，而不只是更多椅子。
collocations: in the waiting room｜在等候室
tip_zh: waiting room 中间有空格。医院、车站都可以用。

meanings_zh: adj. 冷的 | n. 寒冷；感冒
definition_en: having a low temperature | low temperature, or a common illness
example1_en: It is cold in the classroom this morning.
example1_zh: 今天早晨教室里很冷。
example2_en: Cold classrooms in winter make it harder to learn, especially for children who walked a long way.
example2_zh: 冬天寒冷的教室让学习更难，尤其是走了很远路的孩子。
collocations: catch a cold｜感冒 ; cold water｜冷水
tip_zh: cold 作名词是“寒冷”或“感冒”。

definition_en: very small grains of rock, as on a beach
example1_en: The path is covered with sand.
example1_zh: 小路上盖着沙。
example2_en: Sand in the playground drains rain better than bare soil.
example2_zh: 操场上的沙比光土更能排雨。
collocations: a grain of sand｜一粒沙
tip_zh: sand 通常不可数。

definition_en: a path, a rail, or marks left behind
example1_en: She runs on the track after school.
example1_zh: 她放学后在跑道上跑。
example2_en: Keeping track of bus delays shows which routes fail students most often.
example2_zh: 记录公交延误，能显示哪些线路最常让学生失望。
collocations: keep track of｜记录；跟踪 ; on track｜在正轨上
tip_zh: track 作动词是“跟踪”。

definition_en: in or of the north
example1_en: The northern wind made the field feel colder.
example1_zh: 北风让田野感觉更冷。
example2_en: Northern towns may need longer heating, which changes the winter school budget.
example2_zh: 北方城镇可能需要更长的供暖，这会改变冬季的学校预算。
collocations: northern China｜中国北方
tip_zh: northern 是形容词。名词“北方”用 north。

meanings_zh: adj. 保守的 | n. 保守的人
definition_en: not liking change | a person who does not like change
example1_en: The plan is conservative and keeps the old bus.
example1_zh: 这个方案很保守，保留了旧公交。
example2_en: A conservative estimate of the cost is safer than a hopeful one.
example2_zh: 对费用的保守估计，比乐观的估计更安全。
collocations: a conservative estimate｜保守估计
tip_zh: conservative 也可作名词“保守的人”。政治里的 Conservative 常大写。

definition_en: if not
example1_en: We will walk unless it rains.
example1_zh: 除非下雨，否则我们走路去。
example2_en: A river will not recover unless the factories upstream stop the night waste.
example2_zh: 除非上游工厂停止夜间排污，否则河不会恢复。
collocations: unless necessary｜除非必要
tip_zh: unless 等于 if not，本身已含否定，从句里一般不再加 not。

definition_en: very valuable
example1_en: Time before the exam is precious.
example1_zh: 考前的时间很珍贵。
example2_en: A precious seat on the late bus should go to the student who cannot stand.
example2_zh: 晚班车上珍贵的座位应当给不能站着的学生。
collocations: precious to｜对……珍贵
tip_zh: precious 可形容时间、物品或人。用在人身上时要尊重。

meanings_zh: v. 生产；出示 | n. 农产品
definition_en: to make something, or to show it | food that is grown, especially in large amounts
example1_en: The factory produces parts for buses.
example1_zh: 这家工厂生产公交零件。
example2_en: Local farms that produce food for the school can shorten the road from field to canteen.
example2_zh: 为学校生产食物的本地农场，可以缩短从田地到食堂的路。
collocations: produce evidence｜出示证据
tip_zh: 动词重音在后。名词 produce 指农产品，重音在前。

definition_en: having a sour sharp taste, or containing acid | a chemical substance with a sour sharp quality
example1_en: The lab labels every bottle that is acid.
example1_zh: 实验室给每一瓶酸性的东西贴标签。
example2_en: Students learn the word acid and the warning sign, not a method for making it.
example2_zh: 学生学的是 acid 这个词和警告标志，不是制造它的方法。
collocations: acid rain｜酸雨
tip_zh: acid 作名词是酸。本条只作课堂词汇和安全提示，不写制备或使用方法。

definition_en: material burned to produce heat or power
example1_en: The bus runs on cleaner fuel this year.
example1_zh: 今年这辆公交使用更清洁的燃料。
example2_en: Cutting fuel use in old buildings can pay for itself if the windows actually close.
example2_zh: 如果窗户真的能关上，减少旧楼的燃料消耗可以收回成本。
collocations: fossil fuel｜化石燃料
tip_zh: fuel 作物质名词时常不可数。作动词是加燃料或激起。

definition_en: a vehicle with two wheels and an engine
example1_en: A motorcycle was parked across the school gate.
example1_zh: 一辆摩托车横停在校门口。
example2_en: He sold the motorcycle and bought a bicycle after the second fine for speeding.
example2_zh: 第二次超速被罚之后，他卖了摩托车，买了自行车。
collocations: ride a motorcycle｜骑摩托车 ; a motorcycle helmet｜摩托车头盔
tip_zh: motorcycle 是有发动机的两轮车。自行车是 bicycle，还在后面的考纲词里。

definition_en: to keep in the hand, to organise, or to contain
example1_en: Please hold the door for the next person.
example1_zh: 请为后面的人扶住门。
example2_en: A hall that cannot hold the whole school should not be the only place for a fire drill.
example2_zh: 容纳不下全校的礼堂，不该是消防演习的唯一地点。
collocations: hold on｜等一下；坚持 ; hold a meeting｜举行会议
tip_zh: hold 的过去式和过去分词是 held。

definition_en: a person who owns or manages a farm
example1_en: The farmer sells corn on Friday.
example1_zh: 这位农民周五卖玉米。
example2_en: The farmer loaded the corn before the rain started.
example2_zh: 农民在下雨前把玉米装上了车。
collocations: a rice farmer｜稻农
tip_zh: farm 已在本库。

definition_en: the place where visitors are received, or a formal party
example1_en: The reception is by the front door.
example1_zh: 接待处在前门边。
example2_en: A reception for parents should not start after the last bus.
example2_zh: 家长招待会不应当在末班车之后才开始。
collocations: reception desk｜接待处
tip_zh: reception 可数。

definition_en: a hot drink made from coffee beans
example1_en: The teachers drink coffee in the office.
example1_zh: 老师们在办公室喝咖啡。
example2_en: A night of coffee before an exam keeps students awake, and it also makes the next morning harder.
example2_zh: 考前一夜咖啡能让学生醒着，也会让第二天早上更难熬。
collocations: a cup of coffee｜一杯咖啡 ; black coffee｜黑咖啡
tip_zh: coffee 作物质名词不可数。a coffee 可以指一杯咖啡。

definition_en: facing away from the centre, or seeming true only on the surface
example1_en: The outward trip takes two hours.
example1_zh: 去程要两个小时。
example2_en: His outward calm hid a lot of worry, which we noticed only after the exam papers were collected.
example2_zh: 他表面的平静藏着许多担心，我们是在试卷收上去之后才看出来的。
collocations: the outward journey｜去程 ; outward appearance｜外表
word_family: outwardly (adv. 表面上) ; inward (adj. 向内的)
tip_zh: outward journey 是去程，return 是回程。outward appearance 是外表。副词 outwardly 常表示「表面上」。

definition_en: to some degree, not completely
example1_en: The delay was partly the storm.
example1_zh: 这次延误有一部分是因为暴风雨。
example2_en: A plan that only partly names the bus still leaves families guessing.
example2_zh: 只部分写出公交的计划，仍然让家庭在猜。
collocations: partly because｜部分是因为
tip_zh: partly 是副词。

definition_en: a covering for the foot
example1_en: The shoe is under the desk.
example1_zh: 鞋在书桌下面。
example2_en: A wet shoe at the gate is a reason to bring a spare pair.
example2_zh: 门口的湿鞋是再带一双的理由。
collocations: a pair of shoes｜一双鞋
tip_zh: 常用复数 shoes。

definition_en: containing poison, or able to cause illness or death
example1_en: Those red berries are poisonous.
example1_zh: 那些红浆果有毒。
example2_en: The lab label says the leaves are poisonous, so students wear gloves and do not taste them.
example2_zh: 实验标签写明这些叶子有毒，所以学生戴手套，也不去尝。
collocations: poisonous berries｜有毒的浆果 ; a poisonous snake｜毒蛇
word_family: poison (n. 毒物) ; poisonously (adv. 有毒地)
tip_zh: poison 已在库里。poisonous 是形容词。不要把有毒植物写成品尝方法。

definition_en: to take hold of something suddenly, or to take a chance
example1_en: Seize the chance to ask a question.
example1_zh: 抓住提问的机会。
example2_en: She seized the rope with both hands when the boat swung away from the step.
example2_zh: 船离开台阶晃开时，她双手抓住了绳子。
collocations: seize a chance｜抓住机会 ; seize sb by the arm｜抓住某人的胳膊
tip_zh: seize a chance / an opportunity。抓住胳膊是 seize sb by the arm。名词 seizure 在医学里还可以是发作。

definition_en: from another country
example1_en: She is learning a foreign language.
example1_zh: 她在学一门外语。
example2_en: Foreign news is useful only when students also know how to check the source.
example2_zh: 只有当学生也知道如何核对来源时，外国新闻才有用。
collocations: foreign language｜外语 ; foreigner｜外国人
tip_zh: foreign 是形容词，不说 foreign country people，说 people from other countries 或 foreigners。

definition_en: the planet, or soil
example1_en: We live on the earth.
example1_zh: 我们生活在地球上。
example2_en: Healthy earth near a river can hold flood water that concrete sends straight into the street.
example2_zh: 河边健康的土壤能蓄住洪水，而混凝土会把水直接送进街道。
collocations: on earth｜究竟；在地球上
tip_zh: the earth 指地球时常加 the。on earth 也可加强疑问语气。

definition_en: a bicycle
example1_en: I ride my bike when the path is dry.
example1_zh: 路干的时候我骑自行车。
example2_en: A place to lock a bike matters as much as a lesson about clean air.
example2_zh: 一个能锁自行车的地方，和一节关于清洁空气的课一样重要。
collocations: by bike｜骑自行车 ; bike lane｜自行车道
tip_zh: bike 是 bicycle 的口语。by bike 不加冠词。表里没有这一条，本库用 espeak-ng。

definition_en: the reflexive form of they
example1_en: The students organised the fair themselves.
example1_zh: 学生们自己组织了这次义卖。
example2_en: Communities can protect a river themselves, but they still need the law behind them.
example2_zh: 社区可以自己保护一条河，但他们仍然需要法律在背后支持。
collocations: by themselves｜独自
tip_zh: themselves 不能代替 they 作主语。

meanings_zh: adj. 小的；少的 | adv. 少
definition_en: small, or not much | not much
example1_en: There is little time before the bus leaves.
example1_zh: 汽车开走前时间不多了。
example2_en: A little shade on a playground can make summer sports safer for younger children.
example2_zh: 操场上一点点荫凉，就能让年幼的孩子在夏天运动时更安全。
collocations: a little｜一点 ; little by little｜逐渐
tip_zh: little 偏否定，表示几乎没有；a little 表示有一点。都修饰不可数名词。

definition_en: of Europe
example1_en: We read a European folk story.
example1_zh: 我们读了一个欧洲民间故事。
example2_en: European visitors bring money to a town, but they also raise rents if housing is already short.
example2_zh: 欧洲游客给城镇带来钱，但如果住房已经短缺，他们也会推高房租。
collocations: European Union｜欧洲联盟
tip_zh: European 和 Europe 都要大写。

meanings_zh: adj. 甜的；可爱的 | n. 糖果；甜食
definition_en: tasting of sugar, or pleasant | a piece of candy or a sweet dish
example1_en: This tea is too sweet for me.
example1_zh: 这茶对我来说太甜了。
example2_en: A sweet snack every afternoon can hide how much sugar a teenager drinks in a week.
example2_zh: 每天下午一块甜点，会掩盖青少年一周喝下多少糖。
collocations: sweet tooth｜爱吃甜食 ; a sweet voice｜甜美的嗓音
tip_zh: sweet 作名词时常指糖果，英式英语更常见。

definition_en: a feeling of hurt
example1_en: She felt a pain in her knee after the match.
example1_zh: 比赛后她感到膝盖疼。
example2_en: Tooth pain that waits a month for a clinic becomes a larger problem than it was on the first day.
example2_zh: 等了一个月才看上诊所的牙痛，会比第一天更严重。
collocations: in pain｜疼痛 ; a pain in｜……疼
tip_zh: pain 可数或不可数都可以。

definition_en: a long flat surface in a shop or bank
example1_en: Please pay at the counter.
example1_zh: 请在柜台付款。
example2_en: A counter that is too high hides the person who is serving a child.
example2_zh: 太高的柜台会挡住正在给孩子服务的那个人。
collocations: at the counter｜在柜台 ; counter to｜与……相反
tip_zh: counter 作动词是反驳。run counter to 表示与……相反。

definition_en: the early part of the day
example1_en: I review words every morning.
example1_zh: 我每天早晨复习单词。
example2_en: A hot morning in a room without fans makes the first lesson harder than it needs to be.
example2_zh: 没有风扇的房间里炎热的早晨，会让第一节课难上加难。
collocations: in the morning｜在上午 ; morning exercise｜早操
tip_zh: 泛指上午用 in the morning；具体某一天上午用 on Monday morning。

definition_en: a large desert animal with one or two humps
example1_en: A camel rested by the well.
example1_zh: 一头骆驼在井边休息。
example2_en: The textbook compares the hump of a camel with a water store, then warns that the animal still needs real water.
example2_zh: 课本把骆驼的驼峰和储水作比较，接着提醒这种动物仍然需要真正的水。
collocations: a camel caravan｜骆驼商队 ; camel hair｜驼毛
tip_zh: camel 有单峰和双峰。复数 camels。驼峰是 hump。

definition_en: as the representative of someone
example1_en: She spoke on behalf of the class.
example1_zh: 她代表班级发言。
example2_en: A speech on behalf of students should come after someone has asked them.
example2_zh: 代表学生的讲话，应当在有人问过他们之后。
collocations: on behalf of｜代表
tip_zh: 几乎只用于 on behalf of 或 on somebody's behalf。

definition_en: a unit of distance
example1_en: The farm is two miles from school.
example1_zh: 农场离学校两英里。
example2_en: A mile of pavement matters more to a walking student than a faster road with none.
example2_zh: 对步行的学生来说，一英里人行道比没有人行道的更快的路更重要。
collocations: miles away｜很远
tip_zh: 1 mile 约 1.6 公里。英里是 mile，米是 metre。

meanings_zh: prep. 在……外面 | adv. 在外面
definition_en: not inside | outdoors or not inside
example1_en: Please wait outside the office.
example1_zh: 请在办公室外面等。
example2_en: Noise from outside a classroom can undo the quiet a teacher is trying to keep.
example2_zh: 教室外面的噪音可以毁掉老师试图保持的安静。
collocations: outside of｜在……外面
tip_zh: outside 可作介词或副词。

definition_en: in or to a place that is not named
example1_en: I left my bag somewhere in the hall.
example1_zh: 我把包落在大厅的某个地方了。
example2_en: Students need somewhere quiet to read when home has no spare room.
example2_zh: 家里没有空房间时，学生需要一个安静的地方读书。
collocations: somewhere else｜别的地方
tip_zh: somewhere 是副词，前面不加 in。表里这一行的音标是 sometimes，本库不用。

definition_en: what is true
example1_en: Please tell the truth about the broken window.
example1_zh: 请说出打破窗户的真相。
example2_en: The truth about a flood includes which streets were under water, not only the official speech.
example2_zh: 洪水的真相包括哪些街被水淹了，而不只是官方的讲话。
collocations: tell the truth｜说实话 ; in truth｜事实上
tip_zh: truth 通常不可数。

definition_en: a structure that sends water into the air
example1_en: Children play beside the fountain at noon.
example1_zh: 中午孩子们在喷泉边玩。
example2_en: The fountain is turned off in winter, and the basin fills with dry leaves.
example2_zh: 喷泉冬天关掉，水池里积满干叶子。
collocations: a stone fountain｜石喷泉 ; drinking fountain｜饮水台
tip_zh: 喷泉是 fountain。山是 mountain。饮水台也可以叫 drinking fountain。

definition_en: the direction between north and west
example1_en: The wind is from the north-west.
example1_zh: 风从西北来。
example2_en: Villages in the north-west share one clinic, so the winter road between them must stay open.
example2_zh: 西北的村子共用一家诊所，所以它们之间的冬季道路必须保持通畅。
collocations: in the north-west｜在西北
tip_zh: north-west 也可写作 northwest。

meanings_zh: adj. 黑色的 | n. 黑色
definition_en: of the darkest colour | the colour black
example1_en: The black cat slept on the warm step.
example1_zh: 黑猫睡在温暖的台阶上。
example2_en: Black smoke from old buses is a daily health problem for students waiting at the stop.
example2_zh: 旧公交冒出的黑烟，是等车学生每天面对的健康问题。
collocations: black and white｜黑白的
tip_zh: black 也可作名词表示黑色。

definition_en: a game, or the ball used in it
example1_en: Basketball practice is at four.
example1_zh: 篮球训练在四点。
example2_en: A basketball court that locks at dusk leaves the students who finish late outside.
example2_zh: 黄昏就锁上的篮球场，把下课晚的学生留在外面。
collocations: play basketball｜打篮球
tip_zh: 球类运动前通常不加 the：play basketball。

definition_en: a closed path, or a complete electrical path
example1_en: The bus runs a circuit of the town.
example1_zh: 公交绕城镇跑一圈。
example2_en: The lab circuit is drawn on the board, and the switch stays off until the teacher checks it.
example2_zh: 实验室电路画在黑板上，在老师检查之前开关保持关闭。
collocations: a circuit of｜绕……一圈
tip_zh: circuit 可指路线或电路。本条不写如何接通危险电路。

meanings_zh: n. 终点站；终端 | adj. 末端的
definition_en: the end of a route, or a computer screen and keyboard | at the end
example1_en: The bus terminal is at the end of the avenue.
example1_zh: 公交终点站在大街尽头。
example2_en: A computer terminal in the library needs a working clock.
example2_zh: 图书馆的计算机终端需要一块能走的钟。
collocations: bus terminal｜公交终点站
tip_zh: terminal 作形容词可指晚期的。表里这一行的音标是 term，本库不用。

definition_en: the body that goes round the earth
example1_en: The moon was bright on the way home.
example1_zh: 回家的路上月亮很亮。
example2_en: A town that turns off some lights can still see the moon, and the owls can hunt.
example2_zh: 关掉一部分灯的城镇仍然看得见月亮，猫头鹰也能捕猎。
collocations: full moon｜满月
tip_zh: moon 前通常加 the。

definition_en: a large wild cat with stripes
example1_en: The tiger is in the nature book.
example1_zh: 老虎在自然课本里。
example2_en: A lesson about the tiger should say where it can live, not how to harm it.
example2_zh: 关于老虎的课应当说它能住在哪里，而不是如何伤害它。
collocations: a tiger of｜一只老虎
tip_zh: tiger 可数。

definition_en: the Christian festival on 25 December
example1_en: The shop is closed on Christmas Day.
example1_zh: 商店在圣诞节关门。
example2_en: Christmas lights can make a street feel safe at night if they do not replace the ordinary lamps.
example2_zh: 圣诞灯可以让街道在夜里感觉安全，如果它们不是用来代替普通路灯的。
collocations: at Christmas｜在圣诞节 ; Christmas Eve｜平安夜
tip_zh: Christmas 要大写。

definition_en: a table for writing or working
example1_en: Leave the desk clear.
example1_zh: 把书桌收拾干净。
example2_en: A desk at home is not available to every student, which is why the library stays open.
example2_zh: 不是每个学生家里都有书桌，所以图书馆一直开着。
collocations: at the desk｜在书桌前
tip_zh: desk 可数。

definition_en: of the kind already mentioned
example1_en: I have never seen such a clear night sky.
example1_zh: 我从没见过这么晴朗的夜空。
example2_en: Such a small tax on plastic bags can change what millions of shoppers carry home.
example2_zh: 对塑料袋征收如此小的一笔费用，就能改变数百万人拎回家的东西。
collocations: such as｜例如 ; such...that｜如此……以至于
tip_zh: such a/an + 形容词 + 可数名词单数；so + 形容词。

definition_en: kind and soft
example1_en: The rain was gentle all morning.
example1_zh: 整个上午雨都很小。
example2_en: A gentle voice helped the child finish the story.
example2_zh: 轻柔的声音帮孩子把故事读完。
collocations: a gentle slope｜缓坡
tip_zh: gentle 可形容人或动作。

definition_en: a special right given to a person or group
example1_en: A seat by the window felt like a privilege.
example1_zh: 靠窗的位子让人觉得是一种优待。
example2_en: She called the trip a privilege.
example2_zh: 她说这次出行是一种荣幸。
collocations: a special privilege｜一项特权
tip_zh: privilege 可数。

definition_en: to defeat, or to hit repeatedly
example1_en: Our team beat Class Three.
example1_zh: 我们队打败了三班。
example2_en: You cannot beat a flood with a speech if the drains are still too small.
example2_zh: 如果排水管仍然太小，你无法用一篇讲话打败洪水。
collocations: beat sb｜打败某人 ; heartbeat｜心跳
tip_zh: 打败某人用 beat sb；赢得比赛用 win a match。过去式是 beat，过去分词是 beaten。

definition_en: causing public disagreement
example1_en: The plan is controversial.
example1_zh: 这个计划有争议。
example2_en: A controversial fee should be written down before the meeting.
example2_zh: 有争议的费用应当在开会前写下来。
collocations: a controversial topic｜有争议的话题
tip_zh: controversial 形容事物。

definition_en: an act of performing, or how well someone does
example1_en: The music performance starts at seven.
example1_zh: 音乐表演七点开始。
example2_en: A student's performance on one test should not decide the whole story of a year.
example2_zh: 学生一次考试的表现，不该决定一整年的全部故事。
collocations: give a performance｜演出
tip_zh: performance 可指演出，也可指工作或学习表现。

definition_en: to give information to someone, or to recognise a difference
example1_en: Please tell me when the meeting starts.
example1_zh: 请告诉我会议什么时候开始。
example2_en: A label should tell shoppers where food comes from, not only how attractive the packet looks.
example2_zh: 标签应该告诉购物者食物来自哪里，而不只是包装有多好看。
collocations: tell sb to do｜叫某人做 ; tell...from｜把……与……区分 ; tell a story｜讲故事
tip_zh: tell 后面接人：tell sb sth。say 后面接说的内容，不直接接人。

definition_en: money paid regularly for work, often by the month
example1_en: The salary is paid on the first day.
example1_zh: 薪水在每月第一天发。
example2_en: A salary that cannot pay the rent pushes workers away from the school.
example2_zh: 付不起租金的薪水，把工人推离学校。
collocations: a salary of｜……的薪水
tip_zh: salary 多指月薪。wage 是本批的另一词，常指周薪。

definition_en: the sound of speaking, or the right to speak
example1_en: She has a clear voice.
example1_zh: 她的声音很清楚。
example2_en: Students need a voice in decisions about the hour their school day starts.
example2_zh: 关于上学时间的决定，学生需要有发言权。
collocations: in a low voice｜低声 ; raise one's voice｜提高嗓门
tip_zh: voice 多指人的嗓音；sound 是任何声音。

definition_en: a general direction of change
example1_en: The trend is toward later school starts.
example1_zh: 趋势是上学时间更晚。
example2_en: A trend in the numbers is not a plan until someone writes the next step.
example2_zh: 数字里的趋势在有人写下下一步之前还不是计划。
collocations: a trend toward｜朝……的趋势
tip_zh: trend 可数。

definition_en: a series of lessons, or the way something develops
example1_en: I chose a history course this term.
example1_zh: 这学期我选了一门历史课。
example2_en: Of course a new course needs books, but it also needs a teacher who has time to mark them.
example2_zh: 新课程当然需要书，但也需要有时间批改的老师。
collocations: of course｜当然 ; in the course of｜在……过程中
tip_zh: course 表示课程；of course 是固定短语“当然”。

definition_en: a male ruler
example1_en: The story is about a king who listened to farmers.
example1_zh: 故事讲的是一位倾听农民的国王。
example2_en: Even a king in an old tale needed roads and grain, which is still true of any government.
example2_zh: 即使是旧故事里的国王也需要道路和粮食，任何政府今天仍然如此。
collocations: king of｜……之王
tip_zh: king 是可数名词。

definition_en: the ability to learn and understand
example1_en: The quiz does not measure all of a student's intelligence.
example1_zh: 这次小测测不出一名学生的全部智力。
example2_en: Artificial intelligence can sort answers, and a teacher still has to notice who is lost.
example2_zh: 人工智能可以给答案分类，老师仍然得注意到谁没跟上。
collocations: artificial intelligence｜人工智能
tip_zh: intelligence 通常不可数。表示情报时多用于机构名称。

definition_en: low land between hills or mountains
example1_en: Fog stays in the valley in the morning.
example1_zh: 早晨雾留在山谷里。
example2_en: Schools in a valley share one road, so a flood closes more than one gate.
example2_zh: 山谷里的学校共用一条路，所以一场洪水会关上不止一扇校门。
collocations: in the valley｜在山谷里
tip_zh: valley 可数。河流经过的谷地也叫 valley。

definition_en: belonging to us
example1_en: The books on the desk are ours.
example1_zh: 桌上的书是我们的。
example2_en: A room that is ours for one hour still needs to be locked afterwards.
example2_zh: 只属于我们一小时的房间，之后仍然需要锁上。
collocations: a friend of ours｜我们的一个朋友
tip_zh: ours 是名词性物主代词，后面不接名词。限定词 our 作为虚词未单列。

definition_en: to make someone believe
example1_en: She tried to convince him to stay.
example1_zh: 她试图说服他留下来。
example2_en: Governments must convince residents that improved public transport offers a practical alternative to private cars.
example2_zh: 政府必须让居民相信，改善后的公共交通能够切实替代私家车出行。
collocations: convince someone of something｜使某人相信某事 ; convince someone that｜使某人确信 ; convince someone to do something｜说服某人做某事
tip_zh: convince sb of sth表示使某人相信某事。

definition_en: the shore beside the sea
example1_en: We walked on the beach after lunch.
example1_zh: 午饭后我们在海滩上走了走。
example2_en: A popular beach can damage the coast if plastic from one weekend is left in the sand.
example2_zh: 如果一个周末的塑料留在沙子里，受欢迎的海滩会破坏海岸。
collocations: on the beach｜在海滩上
tip_zh: beach 是可数名词。

definition_en: related to literature
example1_en: The literary club meets on Thursday.
example1_zh: 文学社周四见面。
example2_en: A literary text about a flood can start a discussion, and the bus time still has to be fact.
example2_zh: 写洪水的文学作品可以开启讨论，公交时间却必须是事实。
collocations: literary works｜文学作品
tip_zh: literature 已在本库。

definition_en: lower than
example1_en: The temperature fell below zero last night.
example1_zh: 昨夜气温降到了零度以下。
example2_en: Scores below the pass line still show effort, and they should not be the only story of a term.
example2_zh: 低于及格线的分数仍然说明有努力，而且不该成为一学期的唯一故事。
collocations: below zero｜零度以下 ; see below｜见下文
tip_zh: below 强调低于某个水平；under 多指在某物正下方。

meanings_zh: n. 荣誉 | v. 尊敬；授予荣誉
definition_en: great respect, or something that brings it | to show respect, or to give an award
example1_en: It was an honor to speak for the class.
example1_zh: 代表班级发言是一种荣誉。
example2_en: An honor roll that lists only scores misses the student who kept the library open.
example2_zh: 只列分数的光荣榜，会漏掉那个让图书馆一直开着的学生。
collocations: in honor of｜为纪念 ; have the honor of｜有幸
tip_zh: honor 是美式拼写，英式是 honour。作动词是尊敬或授予荣誉。

definition_en: a person's social or legal position
example1_en: The form asks for your student status.
example1_zh: 表格询问你的学生身份。
example2_en: Social status should not decide who may use the public library after school.
example2_zh: 社会地位不该决定谁可以在放学后使用公共图书馆。
collocations: social status｜社会地位 ; status quo｜现状
tip_zh: status 通常不可数。法律地位、社会地位都可以用。

definition_en: to make something less
example1_en: The school wants to reduce food waste.
example1_zh: 学校想减少食物浪费。
example2_en: Cities can reduce traffic near schools by changing the bell, not only by adding lanes.
example2_zh: 城市可以靠调整铃声来减少学校附近的车流，而不只是加车道。
collocations: reduce sth to｜把……减少到 ; reduce by｜减少了
tip_zh: reduce 后接所减少的东西。表里的美式音标不完整，美式读音用 espeak-ng。

definition_en: a married woman
example1_en: His wife teaches at the primary school.
example1_zh: 他的妻子在小学教书。
example2_en: A wife who works nights still needs a safe bus home after the last shift.
example2_zh: 上夜班的妻子在最后一班结束后，仍然需要一趟安全的回家公交。
collocations: husband and wife｜夫妻
tip_zh: wife 的复数是 wives。

definition_en: an idea of how something is
example1_en: The concept is easier with a picture.
example1_zh: 这个概念配上一张图就容易些。
example2_en: Students grasp a new concept faster when they can test it on a familiar problem.
example2_zh: 学生若能用熟悉的题目检验一个新概念，就会理解得更快。
collocations: the concept of｜……的概念
tip_zh: concept 比 idea 更偏学科里的概念。

meanings_zh: n. 恶习 | adj. 副的
definition_en: a bad habit or moral fault | next in rank
example1_en: The essay argues that waste is a public vice.
example1_zh: 文章认为浪费是一种公共恶习。
example2_en: The vice principal, not the principal, meets the bus company on Mondays.
example2_zh: 周一和公交公司见面的是副校长，不是校长。
collocations: vice president｜副总统；副校长
tip_zh: vice 作名词是恶习。放在职称前表示“副”：vice principal。两种意思不要混在一个句子里让人猜。

meanings_zh: v. 希望 | n. 希望
definition_en: to want something to happen | a feeling of wanting something good
example1_en: I hope to see you at the concert.
example1_zh: 我希望在音乐会上见到你。
example2_en: Families hope the new clinic will open before winter, when travel on icy roads is harder.
example2_zh: 家人希望新诊所在冬天前开业，因为结冰的路更难走。
